subject: Computer Networking
title: The 2011 Japan Earthquake and Cables
description: A 60-second lesson on The 2011 Japan Earthquake and Cables.

hook.text: The 2011 Tōhoku earthquake and tsunami damaged multiple undersea cables connecting Japan to the world.

buildup.text: Japan is a major internet hub for Asia-Pacific. Multiple cables landing on its coast were severed.

discovery.text: Traffic rerouted through surviving cables automatically. Redundancy prevented a total outage.

twist.text: Some routes added thousands of extra miles. Latency spiked and bandwidth dropped for weeks.

climax.text: Repairs took months. Cable ships worked in harsh conditions to splice fiber on the ocean floor.

punchline.text: Redundant cables saved Japan's internet. Single-cable nations weren't so lucky.

quiz.question: Why didn't Japan lose internet entirely despite cable damage?
options: Redundant cables allowed traffic to reroute automatically
Satellite internet replaced all cable capacity
The cables were repaired within hours

details.summary: The 2011 Tohoku earthquake and tsunami damaged multiple undersea cables connecting Japan to the rest of the world. Despite the massive physical destruction, internet traffic was rerouted through surviving cables and paths, demonstrating the resilience that redundant cable systems provide.
details.whyItMatters: Japan's experience proved that redundant undersea cable routes can maintain connectivity even during catastrophic events. Redundancy in physical infrastructure saves entire nations from isolation.
takeaways: The earthquake and tsunami damaged multiple undersea cables
Redundant routes maintained Japan's internet connectivity
Japan's cable diversity prevented total disconnection

faq.question: How did Japan's internet survive such massive damage?
faq.answer: Japan connects to the global internet through numerous undersea cables on diverse routes. When some were damaged, traffic shifted to surviving cables. The network was degraded but not disconnected. This diversity is exactly what makes internet infrastructure resilient.

faq.question: What lessons did the 2011 earthquake teach about infrastructure?
faq.answer: It demonstrated that physical redundancy across geographically diverse routes is essential. Countries and companies that rely on a single cable path are vulnerable. The earthquake validated decades of investment in route diversity for the Japanese internet.
